name: Pictured Rocks
unique: Fifteen miles of Lake Superior shoreline streaked with mineral colors, sea caves and arches, best seen from a kayak or the boat tour.
buzz: The kayak tour is the consensus highlight; the water is 40 degrees and the weather changes fast. Book the morning boat.

name: Sleeping Bear Dunes
unique: A 450-foot wall of sand dropping into Lake Michigan, with the Dune Climb, a ghost forest and the Pierce Stocking drive above the water.
buzz: The dune climb is harder than it looks and the run down is the payoff; arrive early for the overlook parking.

name: Detroit Institute of Arts
unique: A encyclopedic museum with the Detroit Industry murals by Diego Rivera, a strong African American collection and a central courtyard.
buzz: The Rivera murals are worth the trip alone, and the collection is deep. Free for local residents on some days.

name: Greenfield Village
unique: A village of historic buildings moved from across the country, including Edison's lab, the Wright brothers' shop and a Model T ride.
buzz: The Model T ride and the Wright shop are the highlights, and the village is huge. Allow half a day.

name: Henry Ford Museum
unique: A museum of American innovation with the Presidential limousine JFK was shot in, the Rosa Parks bus, a giant locomotive and rows of historic cars.
buzz: The bus and the limousine are the emotional artifacts, and the car collection is enormous. Allow three hours.

name: Mackinac Island
unique: A car free Victorian island where you bike an 8-mile loop past limestone arches, fudge shops and the white veranda of the Grand Hotel.
buzz: Everyone bikes the loop and eats fudge; the island is crowded midday and blissful at 8am. Bring cash for the ferry.

name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
unique: Sixty thousand acres of old growth forest on Lake Superior, with waterfalls, a escarpment and backcountry campsites.
buzz: Remote and quiet, with real wilderness and Lake of the Clouds as the view. Bring bug spray.

name: Frederik Meijer Gardens
unique: A 158 acre garden with a butterfly house, a Japanese garden, a children's garden and a large sculpture park.
buzz: The butterfly exhibit is the spring draw and the sculpture park is excellent. Allow half a day.

name: Motown Museum
unique: The modest house where Hitsville USA recorded the Supremes, the Temptations and Stevie Wonder, with the original studio and control room.
buzz: The studio is tiny and the guides sing, which makes it joyful. Book ahead, because tours sell out.

name: Movement Detroit
unique: The festival that anchors Detroit's claim as the birthplace of techno, staged in Hart Plaza with the river and the skyline as the backdrop.
buzz: Lineups are deep and the crowd is serious about the music; after parties are the real scene. Book lodging months ahead.

name: Cranbrook Educational Community
unique: A Saarinen designed campus with a science museum, an art academy and a house by Eliel Saarinen, plus a Japanese garden and a fountain by Carl Milles.
buzz: The art museum and the house are the stops and the gardens are a separate hour; it is a campus rather than a single museum.

name: Tahquamenon Falls
unique: A 50-foot curtain of amber water tinted by cedar tannins, with a lower falls you can row to and a brewpub at the park entrance.
buzz: The upper falls are the photo; the lower falls are the swim. Black flies in June are legendary.

name: ArtPrize
unique: An open entry art competition that takes over an entire city, venues in bars, churches, parks and museums, with the public voting for the winner.
buzz: The scale is the point; some work is amateur and some is museum grade. Download the map and pick three venues.

name: Kitch-iti-kipi
unique: A 40-foot deep spring so clear you can see the bottom from a self propelled raft, with ancient tree trunks and trout suspended in turquoise water.
buzz: It is a 30-minute stop that people remember for years; the raft is free with park entry. Go early to avoid tour buses.

name: Saugatuck Dunes State Park
unique: A thousand acres of forested dunes with a trail to a wild Lake Michigan beach, where the sand hills are 200 feet high.
buzz: The hike in keeps the crowd down and the beach is one of the least developed on the lake; the trail is sandy and the climb back is real.

name: Traverse City Cherry Festival
unique: Eight days of cherry pie, pit spitting contests, air shows and a parade in the cherry capital of the world, on a bay that looks like the Mediterranean.
buzz: The pie and the setting are the draw; traffic is intense. Stay for the sunset over Grand Traverse Bay.

name: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
unique: Zaha Hadid's pleated stainless steel building on the Michigan State campus, showing contemporary art and free to enter.
buzz: The building is the reason to stop and the shows are contemporary and changing; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Heidelberg Project
unique: Two blocks of abandoned houses covered in polka dots, stuffed animals and painted signs, an outdoor art environment that refuses to be gentrified away.
buzz: It is free, strange and deeply personal; respect the residents and don't wander into occupied houses. Best with a local guide.

name: Air Zoo
unique: A hangar of World War II aircraft with flight simulators, a 4D theater and a restored SR-71, plus rides in a open cockpit biplane.
buzz: The simulators and the SR-71 are the family stops and the restoration shop is where enthusiasts linger; it is one of the best aviation museums in the midwest.

name: Detroit Zoo
unique: A zoo with a 1930s art deco entrance, a penguin center and a polar bear habitat, built on 125 acres of woods and designed with moats instead of cages.
buzz: The penguins and the arctic ring are the family stops and the art deco buildings are the architecture; it is big and the train saves walking.

name: Meadow Brook Hall
customer: House tour people, architecture fans, history lovers
unique: A Tudor revival mansion with 110 rooms, hand carved wood and a organ, built by a Dodge heiress and now on a university campus.
buzz: The scale and the craftsmanship are the tour and the holiday events fill it; the house is bigger than people expect.

name: Petoskey State Park
unique: A beach on Little Traverse Bay where the Petoskey stones wash up, fossil coral that polishes into a patterned stone, with dunes and a campground.
buzz: Everyone hunts for Petoskey stones and the best hunting is after a storm; the beach is shallow and good for children.

name: Bell's Brewery
unique: The brewery that helped start the Michigan craft beer scene, with a beer garden, a pub and a tour that explains Two Hearted and the state's hop history.
buzz: Beer people make the pilgrimage and the garden is the summer spot; the tour books out and the pub is family friendly until evening.

name: Kalamazoo Nature Center
unique: Twelve hundred acres of forest, prairie and marsh with a interpretive center, live owls and trails along the Kalamazoo River.
buzz: The trails and the birds of prey are the reasons to come and the center is good with children; the spring migration is the season.

name: Matthaei Botanical Gardens
unique: Three hundred acres of gardens and trails along the Huron River, with a conservatory of arid and tropical plants and a bonsai collection.
buzz: The conservatory is the winter stop and the trails are free; the bonsai and the children's garden are the local favorites.

name: Michigan State Capitol
unique: A post Civil War capitol with a dome covered in copper and a rotunda of Michigan stone, restored to its 1879 appearance.
buzz: The rotunda and the glass floor are the details people remember; tours are free and run on the hour.

name: Zingerman's Delicatessen
unique: A deli that became a food institution, with a case of cheeses, a wall of olive oil and a sandwich list that people argue about.
buzz: The line is part of the experience and the reuben is the standard; the bread and the cheese counter are worth the detour alone.

name: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum
customer: Families with young children, school groups
unique: A science center in a 1907 firehouse with water play, a maker space and a physics floor, scaled for children under ten.
buzz: Parents like that everything can be touched and the water room is the hit; it is small and easiest on weekday mornings.

name: Bronner's Christmas Wonderland
unique: The largest Christmas store in the world, open every day of the year, with 50,000 ornaments and a silent night chapel, in a town that leans into its Bavarian theme.
buzz: It is overwhelming and cheerful; the personalized ornament counter is the reason people come back. Christmas music in July.

name: Potter Park Zoo
unique: A small zoo in a riverfront park with a tiger, a train and a farmyard, run by the county and cheap enough for a spontaneous trip.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for a morning and the train is the hit; the zoo is shaded and never overwhelming.
